newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in a quiet session on Sunday and traders said the market was still looking for direction.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.18 percent, or 3.48 points, to 298.63 on low all-share turnover of 151 million shekels against 175 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.10 percent higher at 304.86.

"Activity continues to be moderate but investors are very optimistic. I believe that one of the main reasons is that investors are waiting for a second wave of public offerings next month," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House was less optimistic.
"The new wave of IPOs will put more pressure on the market. The same amount of money will have to be divided between more shares," he said.
But Weidelfeld predicted the postive trend would continue.
"The market looks good and I believe that the outlook for the market is very positive," he said.
Weisberg said share prices were rising but activity was low.

"The market is still looking for direction...The fact that the number of sellers is low reflects the fact that the mood is optimistic but usually during the summer months the market is more relaxed," Weisberg said.
The most active share was Koor Industries, which fell 0.25 percent to 31,655 on volume of 8.1 million shekels.
Stanley Gold, Shamrock Holdings president and Koor's chairman, said on Thursday that he would propose that Koor spin off its biggest publicly traded subsidiaries to shareholders.

Other active shares included Bank Leumi, which rose 0.75 percent to 562 agorot on turnover of 7.1 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals which climbed 1.75 percent to 438 agorot on volume of 6.6 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
